issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code and Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks or redirects irreversible operations, extending -- and eventually superseding most of -- the existing org-rule-guard.py PreToolUse hook. Two front-ends (a PATH-wrapper binary and native PreToolUse hook adapters) share one engine and a modular pack-per-tool rule set.

## Source of truth for scope
DO NOT read a bead-ID checklist here -- the previous genesis bead was closed precisely because its hardcoded ID list went stale twice (once at the bead-rs rehydration, once at a decomposition split) and bead-rs cannot edit a description to repair it. The live blocker list IS the phase list:

    bead why --id <this-bead-id>      # every open bead blocking completion
    bead list --ready                 # what is actually startable right now

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path: icg-ci pipeline (DONE, closed), release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, self-updater, trust pointer (DONE, closed), release-cutting runbook, and the deploy-location requirement
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, deny-only, both front-ends where applicable
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state (Tier 2)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness (updatedInput, additionalContext, value derivation)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists

## Deliberate deferrals and known-accepted gaps (the fallback role of this bead)
Recorded here because a /plan-to-bead audit decided NOT to fix them, so a later reader does not re-litigate:
1. LEGACY IDs IN BEAD PROSE. Roughly ten open beads still cite dead short-form icg-* IDs in their descriptions (provenance references only). bead-rs cannot edit a description, and recreating ten beads to fix prose was judged worse than leaving it. Trust edges, not prose, when they disagree.
2. REDUNDANT EDGES. ~50 blocker edges are transitively implied by another edge on the same bead. Left in place as documentary; they inflate apparent fan-in if the graph is ever used for critical-path analysis.
3. VALUE-DERIVATION HELPERS keeps its plural title, matching plan.md's own component name, despite failing a strict single-task title test.
4. CRATES.IO as a secondary version-check signal is named in the plan but has no bead -- it is conditional on ever publishing the crate.
5. ORG-RULE-GUARD.PY RULES 1 AND 2 (.github/workflows, kind: Job/CronJob) are not excluded on principle but are not scheduled by any phase, so the realistic end state is a kubectl-only rump PLUS those two, not kubectl-only. Rule 4 (mutating kubectl) is permanently excluded.
6. TWO BEADS LOOK ALREADY SATISFIED by in-flight uncommitted work (test-infrastructure setup and coverage-diff fixtures) but stay open deliberately: the fixtures encode the very schema naming the naming-reconciliation bead is chartered to decide, so closing them now would lock in the un-reconciled shape.
7. PHASE 0 IS LOAD-BEARING. Per plan.md, nothing in later phases is meaningfully tamper-resistant until the deploy-location and release-gating work lands. Two Phase 0 artifacts have ALREADY shipped into agent-writable paths -- see the deploy-location bead, which is why it exists.

issue.description:
CommandRegex, both front-ends, deny-only for v1 (Tier 1 -- stateless, decidable from a single invocation: the command text alone shows whether -a/--all is present, or whether trailing pathspec arguments exist after -m/--message). Denies git commit calls that would commit the entire staged index rather than an explicit path set: git commit -a/--all, and bare git commit -m "..." (or --message) with no trailing pathspec arguments.

This is a distinct gap from CLAUDE.md's existing git-staging rule. That rule already bans git add -A/git add ./git commit -a -- but an agent following it precisely (staging only explicit paths via git add <paths>) can still sweep unrelated pre-staged content into its commit if it then runs a bare git commit -m with no pathspec of its own, since git commit with no path arguments commits the full current index, not just what was just added.

Root incident (2026-08-14, commitgraph, worker claude-code-glm-5-adr018, bead cg-194i4a): git add containers/migration-worker/migrator.py containers/migration-worker/test_migrator.py (correct, precise staging) followed by bare git commit -m "..." produced commit 2bcbfe2, which also included ~430 unrelated lines from containers/queue-api/internal/{server,storage}/blocklist*.go -- pre-staged by a different concurrent NEEDLE worker in the same shared checkout. The worker self-corrected (git reset --soft HEAD~1 plus a clean re-commit passing the same two paths to git commit itself, landing as 1543ae2, verified never pushed to origin) before this rule existed to catch it mechanically -- this bead exists so the correction doesn't have to depend on a worker noticing on its own next time.

Distinct failure mode from Stale-HEAD push guard (irrevers-8cff8cf4): that catches pushing on top of remote state that's since moved. This catches unrelated staged content riding into a commit within the same shared tree, before any push ever happens -- the exact incident class that guard's own description already flags as outside its scope.

Redirect: deny + actionable reason ("pass the same file paths to git commit that you passed to git add -- git commit <paths> -m \"...\""). Not updatedInput: Tier 1 has no memory of what a prior git add in the same session actually staged (that is Tier 2 territory, per Architecture), so the correct pathspec to substitute is not derivable from the git commit call's own text -- per docs/notes/redirect-not-just-block.md, updatedInput is reserved for transformations that preserve intent through a derivable safer mechanism, which this is not. Stays deny with an actionable message, same tier/channel as its git-pack siblings (force-push detection, Stale-HEAD push guard).

Applies to all repos, not just known-shared-checkout ones (user direction 2026-08-14) -- explicit pathspecs on git commit have no real downside in an uncontended repo, so this is not scoped narrowly the way the beads-conjunction check is.

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1 git pack -- also needs Architecture's pack list and Phase 1's rule-set prose updated to name this rule (not yet done as of this bead's creation).
issue.title: git pack: commit-without-pathspec guard

issue.description: Coexistence check between icg and the existing org-rule-guard.py PreToolUse hook. PASS CRITERION, per plan.md lines 537-545: pass on CONSISTENT verdicts (both deny, or both allow); fail ONLY on a divergent verdict (one denies, the other does not). During coexistence icg's image-tag pack and org-rule-guard.py's rule 3 will BOTH fire on the same :latest violation -- that redundant double-deny is expected and harmless, not a failure. PROBE: a :latest tag in a .yaml write -- rule 3 is the only rule both systems are scheduled to cover. DO NOT PROBE WITH: a .github/workflows/ write (rule 1), a kind: Job / kind: CronJob write (rule 2), or a mutating kubectl command (rule 4). Those legitimately diverge because no phase absorbs them -- rule 4 PERMANENTLY, per plan.md 'Explicitly not attempted' (narrowing it would need live cluster state, trading away the zero-I/O determinism that makes the blanket block trustworthy). Rule 5 (credential values) is only PARTIALLY absorbed: Phase 1's irrevers-ef9a4767 takes the Bash-channel half while the Write/Edit half stays with org-rule-guard.py, so a Write/Edit credential probe also legitimately diverges. Interim check pending org-rule-guard.py's partial deprecation; proves only the tested case. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 5 + Overview, docs/notes/existing-enforcement-infrastructure.md.

issue.description: Recreated from irrevers-2e1c5a48, which specified the PASS CONDITION BACKWARDS. The old bead asked to 'confirm exactly one system reports the denial, not both redundantly' -- plan.md lines 537-545 says the opposite, deliberately: during coexistence icg's image-tag pack and org-rule-guard.py's rule 3 will BOTH fire on the same :latest violation, and that redundant double-deny is expected and harmless. CORRECT CRITERION: pass on CONSISTENT verdicts (both deny, or both allow); fail ONLY on a divergent verdict (one denies, the other does not) -- divergence is the actual conflict worth catching. PROBE: a :latest tag in a .yaml write, i.e. the rule icg actually absorbs. Do NOT probe with a .github/workflows/ write or a kind: Job write -- org-rule-guard.py rules 1, 2 and 5 are outside icg's scheduled coverage (5 permanently, per 'Explicitly not attempted'), so those legitimately diverge and would fail a correctly-written test. Interim check pending org-rule-guard.py's eventual partial deprecation; proves only the tested case. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 5 + Overview, docs/notes/existing-enforcement-infrastructure.md.
issue.title: Install-time smoke test vs org-rule-guard.py

issue.description: Before allowing git push, compare the local checkout's tracked remote HEAD against the actual current remote HEAD (live check); if they differ, fail the push and redirect the agent to pull and resolve first. Simpler revision of the original shared-tree-collision idea (cross-process /proc scanning), per user direction 2026-08-13. Catches a different failure mode than the documented git-index-race incident (that one was uncommitted work getting swept into another worker's commit within the SAME shared tree, before any push) -- this catches pushing on top of state that's since moved. Deliberate, scoped exception to the no-I/O-in-hot-path engine constraint: git push is already a network operation, so a live remote-HEAD check here doesn't set a precedent for adding I/O to other guarded commands. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #2 (revised mechanism).
issue.title: Stale-HEAD push guard

issue.description: Architecture lines 49-71 promise the engine 'fails open on any parse failure or exception ... matching org-rule-guard.py's exact behavior' -- a missed violation is recoverable, a stuck fleet is not. The plan explicitly separates this IN-PROCESS guarantee from irrevers-cd3f4c44's process-death policy (that one graduates to fail-closed over time; this one never does). cd3f4c44 had a bead, this had none. Scope: every check path wrapped so a throw, a malformed stdin payload, an unreadable rule pack, or a bad regex yields allow, never deny and never a crash. Acceptance: a malformed-stdin fixture and a corrupt-rule-pack fixture both exit allow, wired as Layer 1 regression cases so the guarantee cannot silently regress. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture 'fail-open guarantee'.
issue.title: Engine: unconditional fail-open on parse failure or exception

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md (562 lines, 5 gap-review rounds complete as of 2026-08-13)

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks/redirects irreversible operations, extending org-rule-guard.py's coverage. Full decomposition: 44 beads total (28 created directly from Phase 0-3's plan content, plus 16 pre-existing beads from two /plan-idea-gen ideation runs, retroactively wired with blocker edges to the infrastructure they actually depend on).

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path (icg-ci pipeline, release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, self-updater, release-cutting runbook): 6 beads (icg-4me, icg-52j, icg-1dk, icg-4nu, icg-2nw, icg-24g)
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, both front-ends where applicable: 8 infrastructure beads (icg-4vq, icg-2jd, icg-1k0, icg-3my, icg-3q6, icg-6bg, icg-rik, icg-51o) + 8 new content-pack beads (icg-6tj, icg-1bav, icg-4bra, icg-25sg, icg-4nt2, icg-14ff, icg-u34c, icg-shs8) + 2 pre-existing content beads (icg-2m8 git stale-HEAD, icg-1vj misc deprecated-bead-CLI)
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state: 3 beads (icg-1seg state-store, icg-2eu0 flush-before-pull, icg-20ja flush-before-repair)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness: 3 beads (icg-25u2 updatedInput force-push, icg-50ya additionalContext+Codex-fallback, icg-4338 value-derivation helpers)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists: 9 pre-existing beads (icg-rri, icg-ncf, icg-2ck, icg-l75, icg-1tj, icg-z5n, icg-2i8, icg-59u, icg-d3i)
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists: 6 pre-existing beads (icg-4p8, icg-2m8 [counted in Phase 1], icg-4bu, icg-3xz, icg-4mu, icg-53q) + 1 done directly (README non-goals section, no bead)

## Flagged gap from decomposition review (fallback role, per user direction)
One real gap found reviewing plan.md against the 44-bead decomposition: icg-4bu's fail-closed transition has an explicit open implementation question in Architecture (docs/plan/plan.md lines ~73-87) -- whether Claude Code's/Codex's own hook-timeout/hook-error config can substitute for a dedicated watchdog process, avoiding the 'standing daemon' architecture ideation explicitly killed elsewhere (Lens-1 idea #69). This verification step (checking both harnesses' actual hook specs) isn't its own trackable bead anywhere -- it's prose inside icg-4bu's blocking Architecture discussion. Whoever picks up icg-4bu should do this verification FIRST, before assuming a watchdog is needed; if neither harness supports it, icg-4bu needs to either accept the standing-daemon cost or get re-scoped. Not spinning up a separate bead for this since it's a research step gating one specific bead's approach, not independent work -- flagged here instead per genesis-bead-as-fallback role.

Everything else reviewed against plan.md's Architecture/Components/Data Models/Phases sections maps cleanly onto an existing bead -- no other coverage gaps found.

Measuring a rate across invocations requires persistence in a per-invocation architecture, which nothing in the graph provided. The Overview is explicit that this project only improves on org-rule-guard.py's self-edit gap 'if the deploy-location and release-gating requirements are actually implemented, not just designed', and Phase 0 says nothing in later phases is meaningfully tamper-resistant until this lands. Every other Phase 0 bead covers release GATING; none covered WHERE the artifacts live or who can write them. ALREADY DRIFTING: the shipped src/trust_pointer.rs writes to XDG_CONFIG_HOME/icg/trust-pointer.json and the in-flight self-updater targets dirs::data_local_dir()/icg/rule-pack.json -- both owned by and writable by the same user the guarded agent runs as, i.e. exactly shape 1. Scope: decide and implement install path, ownership and mode for the binary, the rule-pack artifact and the trust pointer; revisit the two paths already chosen. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture + Phase 0.

issue.description: Recreated from irrevers-0f49129d, which bundled measurement with reaction. Measurement now lives in irrevers-b6579270 (per-release deny-rate telemetry and rolling baseline), which has a second consumer in irrevers-cd3f4c44's graduation signal. Scope here is the reaction only: when telemetry reports a fresh release's deny rate spiking above the rolling baseline within the first M commands, auto-revert the self-update trust pointer to the prior release and log loudly. Closes the gap where a bad release silently degrades the whole fleet at once. Kill-pass objection to keep visible: the trigger must be conservative -- a legitimately bad day of command hygiene must not be mistaken for a bad release. Deliberately asymmetric with plan.md Phase 0's hot-reload decision: adopting a release forward is manual, reverting a bad one stays automatic. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 4, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md finalist #3.
issue.title: Poison-pill auto-rollback: revert the trust pointer on a deny-rate spike
